Wedding Node: [Fill in the scene, e.g., Engagement / Main Wedding Ceremony / Toasting / Banquet / Departure / Wedding Reception]

Main Color Scheme: [Fill in the main colors, e.g., Moon White, Jade White, Light Gold / Deep Vermilion Red, Warm Gold / Vermilion Red, Cream White / Ink Black, Dark Gold, Deep Indigo Blue]

Wedding Anchor Point: [Fill in the element, e.g., Veil / Marriage Certificate / Ring Box / Small Bouquet / Phoenix Hairpin / Red Satin / Wedding Cup / Toasting Cup / Jewelry / Floral Window Shadow]

The overall style is Eastern ink fashion illustration, combining new Chinese-style haute couture wedding attire, wedding campaign, rice paper texture, ink brush blank space, semi-transparent gauze layers, fine gold thread depiction, and modern Eastern aesthetics.

The central figure in the image is a slender and elegant Eastern woman, with a high-end, serene, restrained, dignified, or cool temperament. The character's pose must serve the wedding attire display: [Fill in the pose, e.g., Half-side profile adjusting veil / Standing tall to showcase main wedding dress / Looking back lightly raising toasting cup / Standing pose displaying black gold banquet dress]. The character's appearance should resemble an Eastern muse from high-end wedding brand posters, not influencer faces, not cheap ancient style feel, not studio portrait vibe.

The wedding attire must be the visual protagonist of the image. Please emphasize the structure and craftsmanship details of the attire, such as collar structure, shoulder and neck lines, waistband, shawl, cuffs, hemline, veil, semi-transparent gauze layers, pearl embroidery, gold thread phoenix patterns, floral branch motifs, black gold lotus patterns, fine gold thread outlining, fabric draping, and ink wash gradation. The wedding attire should have a modern haute couture feel, not rendered as ordinary ancient costume or studio wedding gown.

The background should be "white but not empty," using extremely light rice paper texture, shallow mist layers, faint ink aura layers, low-saturation gradients, and minimal Eastern wedding imagery. Ink elements should serve the wedding attire: they can be incorporated into the veil, shawl, red satin, hemline, phoenix feathers, floral branches, gold thread traces, and background aura layers, creating a high-end, ethereal, and exquisite Eastern wedding atmosphere.

Overall image requirements: High-end, clean, exquisite, Eastern, light luxury, with a sense of ceremony. From afar, it should evoke a wedding brand campaign feel; up close, it should reveal gauze layers, gold threads, embroidery, wedding anchor points, and ink details.

No text, no signatures, no logos, no watermarks, no copyright information, no complex indoor backgrounds, no collages. Generate only one independent image each time.

prompt_records.prompt_text:
Please generate an original Eastern fashion illustration in 9:16 vertical format, with the theme of [Theme Name].  
Overall style fusion: Modern Eastern haute couture, Chinese ink wash, light watercolor, delicate calligraphy-style lines, rice paper blank space, high-fashion poster aesthetic.  
The image's temperament should be [Temperament Keywords: such as ethereal / cool elegance / light luxury / graceful / lively / serene / modern Eastern].

[1. Character Setting]  
The main subject is a slender and elegant Eastern woman, with refined features, a calm expression, and the muse-like temperament of high-fashion illustration.  
Hairstyle is [Hairstyle: such as low updo / half-tied hair / structured updo / soft bun], with a small amount of natural loose strands.  
Pose is [Pose: such as seated / standing still / looking back / light dance / turning / high-fashion stance], with the composition retaining ample breathing room—do not overcrowd.

[2. Clothing Setting]  
The outfit is an original new Chinese-style haute couture gown, modern Eastern long skirt, or high-fashion piece inspired by qipao elements.  
The overall silhouette is slender, lightweight, and fluid, incorporating [Clothing Elements: such as semi-transparent gauze layers / flowing ribbons / water sleeves / train / high collar / side slit / structured waistline / asymmetrical cut].  
Main clothing color palette is [Clothing Main Color Scheme: such as moon white + light mist blue-gray + soft gold / ink black + deep indigo blue + cool white / celadon green + jade white + light silver / beige white + low-saturation cinnabar red + light gold].  
The clothing naturally integrates with Eastern imagery, including [Main Imagery: such as moon halo / water ripples / flower shadows / feathers /仙鹤 (immortal crane) / cloud vapors / mountain mist / silk ribbons / wind traces].  
These imagery elements should blend into the hemline, train, draped layers, background atmosphere, and local details, rather than being stiff decorations.

[3. Silk Stockings Setting]  
The legs are paired with ultra-thin, semi-transparent, misty-lightweight high-end silk stockings, with a delicate, skin-close texture and a soft, restrained subtle sheen—neither heavy, overly glossy, nor cheap-looking.  
Stockings color is [Stockings Color: such as moon white gray / smoky black gray / light mist blue-gray / pale blue-gray / ivory gray / deep indigo gray].  
The stockings surface features highly restrained exquisite patterns, such as [Stockings Patterns: such as ultra-fine gold thread water ripple texture / petal line sketch / feather veins / vine subtle texture / moon motifs / cloud motifs / light ink gradient / cinnabar fine line texture].  
The stockings should naturally integrate with the overall outfit and ink wash style, highlighting the elongated leg lines and fashion refinement, without overpowering the scene or veering into garish, photorealistic sensuality.

[4. Lines and Details]  
Overall lines should be fine, light, and exquisite, with the main contours using ink lines with a brush calligraphy feel, featuring slight variations in thickness, flying white effects, tapered ends, and elegant flow.  
Incorporate restrained exquisite details locally, such as: fine gold threads, light silver threads, hem edging, feather veins, petal textures, water ripple fine lines, transparent gauze layered shadows, subtle embroidery textures, and internal pleat lines.  
The image should appear lightweight and translucent from afar, with details visible up close.

[5. Background and Blank Space]  
Background uses [Background Base Color: such as light warm white / beige white / rice paper white / cool white].  
Avoid pure dead white; include extremely subtle rice paper texture, light mist feel, faint ink wash atmosphere layers, and gentle light-dark transitions to achieve "white yet not empty."  
Retain ample blank space—do not overcrowd the background or fill the composition.

[6. Ink Wash Expression]  
The ink wash elements should be free-spirited yet controlled, with hierarchy, gradations of density, diffusion, flying white edges, and interspersed blank space.  
Avoid messiness and disorder, large smudged patches, or heavy splashed ink effects.

[7. Overall Requirements]  
The entire image should resemble a high-end Eastern fashion visual poster, balancing exquisite craftsmanship with ink wash charm.  
The composition should be refined, elegant, modern, light luxury, Eastern, and artistic.  
Do not include text, signatures, logos, watermarks, or copyright information.  
Do not copy existing works.  
Avoid thick lines, cheap costume vibes, excessive patterns, hyper-realism, or overcrowded backgrounds.  
Generate each image independently—do not merge.

prompt_records.prompt_text:
Generate a completely original illustration from the "Inkline Couture" series of Eastern fashion, in a 9:16 vertical format.

Overall style fusion: modern Eastern haute couture, Chinese ink aesthetics, light watercolor texture, delicate calligraphy-style lines, and sophisticated large areas of negative space. The image should exude a poetic, understated luxury, ethereal, elegant, refined, and timeless quality.

The background should not be a stark pure white, but instead use a very pale warm white, off-white, or rice paper white as the base, with an extremely subtle rice paper texture, faint paper grain, barely-there mist, ink layering, and slight tonal variations. The overall effect should achieve "white yet not empty," preserving ample breathing room, but never appearing crowded, messy, overfilled, or cluttered.

The central figure is a graceful, slender Eastern woman with a lithe build, poised demeanor, and serene expression, embodying the essence of high-fashion illustration. She should resemble a modern Eastern haute couture muse, not an ordinary ancient-style beauty or realistic influencer portrait. Her facial features should be exquisitely clean and refined, with delicate contours, restrained makeup, soft gaze, and an aura of cool reserve, subtlety, and elegance. Her hairstyle should be naturally sophisticated, such as a low chignon, structured updo, half-tied style, or flowing tendrils with a sense of movement, accented by a few naturally loose strands.

The garment design should be an original neo-Chinese haute couture gown, modern Eastern long dress, or high-fashion piece inspired by qipao elements. The overall silhouette should be elongated, lightweight, fluid, and thoughtfully designed. The clothing may incorporate: semi-transparent gauze layers, airy water sleeves, flowing ribbons, trains, structured waistlines, refined necklines, asymmetrical couture cuts, and more. The attire must avoid any cheap theatrical costume vibe and instead evoke an Eastern gown from high-fashion illustration.

Allow the garment, sleeve hems, ribbons, skirt edges, or train to gradually blend into poetic ink imagery, such as: celestial cranes, feathers, cloud wisps, lunar rings, water ripples, floral shadows, ink petals, silk ribbons, mountain mists, wind traces, and the like. These motifs should grow naturally from the clothing and atmosphere, not feel like rigidly applied decorations.

Lines should be fine, light, and exquisite. The main contours should use ink lines with a brush calligraphy feel, featuring subtle variations in thickness, tapered ends, dry brush effects, and elegant flow, but never heavy, boldly black, or disordered. Local details may include ultra-fine gold threads, pale silver lines, hem edging, feather veins, petal textures, water ripple patterns, subtle embroidered motifs, internal pleat lines, layered gauze shadows, and more—to offer intricate craftsmanship on close inspection, while remaining restrained overall.

The ink elements should be both free-spirited and controlled. Ink tones should have layered relationships: one or two slightly deeper dense ink areas locally as visual focal points, gradually diffusing outward, interwoven with light ink, water marks, dry brush edges, and negative space. Avoid ink becoming muddy, chaotic, excessively splashed, or disorderly in spread.

For color, employ low-saturation, Eastern-inspired, sophisticated palettes, such as: celadon green, jade white, moon white, pale gray-blue, warm ivory, desaturated vermilion red, ink black, deep indigo, soft gray, restrained pale gold, and the like. Color transitions should be gentle, naturally shifting from deep to light. Accent colors should be used sparingly, appearing only in small areas like lips, earrings, ribbons, hems, moonlight, water patterns, petal outlines, or localized gilding.

Composition should maintain a vertical orientation, airy transparency, generous negative space, and a fashion poster sensibility. The figure may be in a standing pose, seated, glancing back, turning, in motion, or still, but with ample breathing room preserved. The entire image should feel like a high-end Eastern fashion visual poster, not an ordinary decorative illustration.

Final mood keywords: refined, poetic, modern, elegant, lightweight, restrained, Eastern, understated luxury, artistic. The whole piece should balance exquisite craftsmanship with ink-wash lyricism.

The overall effect should achieve "white yet not empty," preserving ample breathing room, but never appearing crowded, messy, overfilled, or cluttered.
The central figure is a graceful, slender Eastern woman with a lithe build, poised demeanor, and serene expression, embodying the essence of high-fashion illustration.
She should resemble a modern Eastern haute couture muse, not an ordinary ancient-style beauty or realistic influencer portrait.
Her facial features should be exquisitely clean and refined, with delicate contours, restrained makeup, soft gaze, and an aura of cool reserve, subtlety, and elegance.
Her hairstyle should be naturally sophisticated, such as a low chignon, structured updo, half-tied style, or flowing tendrils with a sense of movement, accented by a few naturally loose strands.
The garment design should be an original neo-Chinese haute couture gown, modern Eastern long dress, or high-fashion piece inspired by qipao elements.
The overall silhouette should be elongated, lightweight, fluid, and thoughtfully designed.
The clothing may incorporate: semi-transparent gauze layers, airy water sleeves, flowing ribbons, trains, structured waistlines, refined necklines, asymmetrical couture cuts, and more.
The attire must avoid any cheap theatrical costume vibe and instead evoke an Eastern gown from high-fashion illustration.

Allow the garment, sleeve hems, ribbons, skirt edges, or train to gradually blend into poetic ink imagery, such as: celestial cranes, feathers, cloud wisps, lunar rings, water ripples, floral shadows, ink petals, silk ribbons, mountain mists, wind traces, and the like.
These motifs should grow naturally from the clothing and atmosphere, not feel like rigidly applied decorations.
Lines should be fine, light, and exquisite.

The main contours should use ink lines with a brush calligraphy feel, featuring subtle variations in thickness, tapered ends, dry brush effects, and elegant flow, but never heavy, boldly black, or disordered.

Local details may include ultra-fine gold threads, pale silver lines, hem edging, feather veins, petal textures, water ripple patterns, subtle embroidered motifs, internal pleat lines, layered gauze shadows, and more—to offer intricate craftsmanship on close inspection, while remaining restrained overall.
The ink elements should be both free-spirited and controlled.

Ink tones should have layered relationships: one or two slightly deeper dense ink areas locally as visual focal points, gradually diffusing outward, interwoven with light ink, water marks, dry brush edges, and negative space.
Avoid ink becoming muddy, chaotic, excessively splashed, or disorderly in spread.

Color transitions should be gentle, naturally shifting from deep to light.
Accent colors should be used sparingly, appearing only in small areas like lips, earrings, ribbons, hems, moonlight, water patterns, petal outlines, or localized gilding.

prompt_records.section_title: 3D Historical Figures Standing Statue Archives - Awakening the Soul of Poetry
prompt_records.prompt_text:
Please create a highly finished **“Historical Figure Breakout Standing Portrait Archive / 3D Historical Breakout Biography Poster.”**

**User Input**
Subject figure: **[Name of the figure]**
Character identity: **[Emperor / Famous General / Statesman / Thinker / Writer / Reformer / Military Strategist, etc.]**
Historical background: **[Dynasty / Historical period]**
Core keywords: **[Unification / Reform / Loyalty and Righteousness / Unity of Knowledge and Action / Northern Expedition / Institutions / School of Mind / Prosperous Era, etc.]**
Main color tendency: **[Black, gold, and red / Cyan-blue, gray, and gold / Dark red, ink, and gold / Iron armor and deep blue, etc.]**
Aspect ratio: **[3:4 vertical]**

This is not an ordinary historical poster. It is a highly finished historical biography poster built around the core structure of **“a central full-body 3D historical figure + a breakout forward-thrusting action + lightweight floating historical event clusters around the figure + a subtle chronological timeline at the bottom.”**

At the center of the image, there must be a complete full-body, standing 3D historical figure. The figure is the most important visual focus of the entire image, with a strong sense of volume, sculptural presence, monumentality, and historical aura. The clothing, headwear, armor, patterns, belt, footwear, accessories, and ornaments must match the figure’s historical period and social identity. The overall style should be realistic, weighty, and cinematic. Beneath the figure’s feet, there should be a light but stable monument-like pedestal that supports the figure without feeling too heavy or overwhelming the composition.

The figure must not be merely standing still. There must be a clear **“forward-thrusting breakout action.”** The hand, arm, or key prop held by the figure — such as a jade seal, imperial edict, scroll, long spear, sword, military tally, court tablet, map, or book — must extend toward the viewer, creating a strong sense of near-large/far-small perspective, front-to-back depth, compressed perspective, and 3D impact as if breaking out of the frame. Pay special attention: the key prop thrusting forward must be fully visible, clear, and recognizable. It must not be cropped so that only a small fragment remains.

Around the figure, arrange **6 to 10 key historical milestones.** Do not make them into heavy, regular, neatly tiled small cards. Instead, present them as **lightweight, floating, multi-directional, semi-transparent historical event clusters.** Each milestone may consist of 2 to 4 sub-fragments, including a number, year, event title, brief description, small historical scene image, fine gold lines, open-frame borders, node dots, annotation lines, and similar elements. The overall feeling should resemble historical archives dismantled into light time-slice fragments, floating and unfolding around the figure, rather than a conventional information-card layout.

These event clusters should have different orientations and spatial perspectives: some tilted left, some tilted right, some turned inward, some flipped outward, some positioned higher, some lower, with front-back layering. They may also be slightly occluded by the figure’s arm, robe hem, or weapon to create spatial depth. They should have a glass-like or acrylic-like quality, subtle glowing edges, incomplete borders, and lightly misaligned layered fragments. The information should be detailed, but visually light, and must not overpower the central figure.

On the left side of the image, place a large title: **[Name of the figure]**. Use a font with an East Asian historical atmosphere, such as calligraphic, stele-inscription, or ink-brush styling. Nearby, you may add birth and death years, identity tags, keyword summaries, and a highly condensed subtitle. The title area should feel stable, simple, and restrained. Do not overcrowd it.

At the bottom, there must be a lightweight, clean, and refined horizontal timeline connecting the important years of the figure’s life, corresponding to the surrounding historical event clusters. The timeline should resemble a curated exhibition guide line, museum time scale, or historical index line. It may use fine gold lines, small dots, concise years, small text labels, and a few decorative nodes. Do not make it into a heavy black horizontal bar or a huge bottom information block.

The background should be based on off-white rice paper, aged paper, old archive paper, or a pale museum wall. The overall tone should be low-saturation, clean, and restrained. You may add subtle map textures, silhouettes of ancient architecture, document fragments, seals, golden connecting lines, annotation lines, nodes, territory outlines, and similar elements to create a light, rational historical archive exhibition atmosphere.

The entire image must establish a clear contrast:

The central figure should be heavy, realistic, three-dimensional, strongly lit, and strongly volumetric.
The surrounding historical nodes should be thin, transparent, floating, subtly glowing, refined, and rational.
The figure’s action should thrust forward and break out of the frame, creating spatial explosive force.
The bottom timeline should remain lightweight and restrained, only serving to organize and conclude the information.

If different requirements conflict, prioritize the following:

1. The central figure must be complete and full-body.
2. The forward-thrusting prop must be fully visible and have strong 3D impact.
3. The surrounding event clusters must be lightweight and floating, not heavy cards.
4. The central figure should feel “heavy,” while the information system should feel “light.”
5. The bottom timeline should be lightweight, clear, and not overpower the image.

If the model has difficulty precisely controlling a large amount of small text, prioritize making the figure’s name, years, numbers, and event titles clear. Short explanatory text may be simplified or left as space for later layout editing.

There must be a clear **“forward-thrusting breakout action.”** The hand, arm, or key prop held by the figure — such as a jade seal, imperial edict, scroll, long spear, sword, military tally, court tablet, map, or book — must extend toward the viewer, creating a strong sense of near-large/far-small perspective, front-to-back depth, compressed perspective, and 3D impact as if breaking out of the frame.
Pay special attention: the key prop thrusting forward must be fully visible, clear, and recognizable.
It must not be cropped so that only a small fragment remains.
Around the figure, arrange **6 to 10 key historical milestones.** Do not make them into heavy, regular, neatly tiled small cards.

Instead, present them as **lightweight, floating, multi-directional, semi-transparent historical event clusters.** Each milestone may consist of 2 to 4 sub-fragments, including a number, year, event title, brief description, small historical scene image, fine gold lines, open-frame borders, node dots, annotation lines, and similar elements.
The overall feeling should resemble historical archives dismantled into light time-slice fragments, floating and unfolding around the figure, rather than a conventional information-card layout.

These event clusters should have different orientations and spatial perspectives: some tilted left, some tilted right, some turned inward, some flipped outward, some positioned higher, some lower, with front-back layering.
They may also be slightly occluded by the figure’s arm, robe hem, or weapon to create spatial depth.
They should have a glass-like or acrylic-like quality, subtle glowing edges, incomplete borders, and lightly misaligned layered fragments.
The information should be detailed, but visually light, and must not overpower the central figure.
On the left side of the image, place a large title: **[Name of the figure]**.
Use a font with an East Asian historical atmosphere, such as calligraphic, stele-inscription, or ink-brush styling.
Nearby, you may add birth and death years, identity tags, keyword summaries, and a highly condensed subtitle.
The title area should feel stable, simple, and restrained.
Do not overcrowd it.
At the bottom, there must be a lightweight, clean, and refined horizontal timeline connecting the important years of the figure’s life, corresponding to the surrounding historical event clusters.
The timeline should resemble a curated exhibition guide line, museum time scale, or historical index line.
It may use fine gold lines, small dots, concise years, small text labels, and a few decorative nodes.
Do not make it into a heavy black horizontal bar or a huge bottom information block.
The background should be based on off-white rice paper, aged paper, old archive paper, or a pale museum wall.
The overall tone should be low-saturation, clean, and restrained.

You may add subtle map textures, silhouettes of ancient architecture, document fragments, seals, golden connecting lines, annotation lines, nodes, territory outlines, and similar elements to create a light, rational historical archive exhibition atmosphere.
The entire image must establish a clear contrast:
The central figure should be heavy, realistic, three-dimensional, strongly lit, and strongly volumetric.
The surrounding historical nodes should be thin, transparent, floating, subtly glowing, refined, and rational.
The figure’s action should thrust forward and break out of the frame, creating spatial explosive force.
The bottom timeline should remain lightweight and restrained, only serving to organize and conclude the information.
If different requirements conflict, prioritize the following:
The central figure must be complete and full-body.
The forward-thrusting prop must be fully visible and have strong 3D impact.
The surrounding event clusters must be lightweight and floating, not heavy cards.
The central figure should feel “heavy,” while the information system should feel “light.”
The bottom timeline should be lightweight, clear, and not overpower the image.
If the model has difficulty precisely controlling a large amount of small text, prioritize making the figure’s name, years, numbers, and event titles clear.
Short explanatory text may be simplified or left as space for later layout editing.

prompt_records.prompt_text:
Generate an image in the style of "Paper Comes to Life · Eastern Wedding Attire," 4:5 vertical format.

The theme is [Phoenix Crown and Rosy Cape / Dragon-Phoenix Robe / Xiuhe Dress / Song Dynasty Wedding Attire]. The scene depicts a high-end off-white wedding gown concept sketch clipped to a wooden drawing board, placed on a warm wood-toned design workbench. The main subject is a photorealistic Chinese bride naturally awakening from the wedding gown concept sketch on the paper.

The character must be extremely photorealistic, like real-life portrait photography, with fair but natural skin featuring authentic skin textures—no anime style, silicone feel, or plastic skin. Her gaze interacts with the lens, dignified and captivating, as if she has just awakened from the wedding gown sketch.

The character's upper body clearly rises from the paper surface, not as a flat illustration. The head, shoulders and neck, chest, waist, arms, and hands have realistic volume, spatial depth, and natural projections. One hand lightly props against the paper surface, creating the illusion of "paper comes to life."

The character's proportions are slender yet natural, approximately 7–7.5 head lengths. The legs, calves, and feet maintain photorealistic texture and natural structure—no line art, no overly thin or thick calves, no disproportionately short lower body.

The attire is a haute couture Eastern wedding gown design, embodying the dignified, elegant, and ceremonial essence of traditional Chinese bridal wear. It may include elements such as phoenix crown, rosy cape, dragon-phoenix patterns, knotted buttons, embroidery, round fan, hanging silk ribbons, pearl hair accessories, gold thread trims, and more. Possible annotations: phoenix crown structure, rosy cape flow, dragon-phoenix motifs, knotted button positions, skirt drape flow, unfinished skirt corners.

The workbench includes red-and-gold cards, pearl accessories, embroidered fabric swatches, gold thread fabric pieces, pencils, dip pens, ceramic teacup, and small motif sketch cards. 4. Beauty close-up cover
   Use a close-up face or side profile, refined skin texture, soft lighting, elegant magazine-cover typography and a premium beauty campaign feeling.

Keep the image stylish, readable and high-end. Avoid cheap e-commerce style, clutter, weak typography, random decorations, fake plastic skin, bad anatomy, distorted products, messy text and real copyrighted magazine logos.

Generate one finished poster only.

prompt_records.section_title: AI Fashion Visual Systems Vol.01 - fashion editorial visual system!
prompt_records.prompt_text:
Use this as a single-image prompt template.
If you want multiple images, generate each one separately. Do not merge them into one collage unless the chosen direction is specifically a lookbook collage spread.

 Direction Type: [Giant typography campaign / Couture magazine cover / Accessories editorial page / Lookbook collage spread]
 Brand Name: [BRAND]
 Theme / Collection: [THEME]
 Product / Focus: [PRODUCT OR SUBJECT]
 Model: [MODEL DESCRIPTION or “no full model, product-focused”]
 Brand Mood: [MINIMAL / QUIET LUXURY / MODERN / ROMANTIC / SHARP / COOL / SOFT / AVANT-GARDE]
 Color Palette: [COLORS]
 Main Headline: [HEADLINE]
 Subheadline: [SUBHEADLINE]
 Extra Small Text: [OPTIONAL SHORT TEXT]
 Aspect Ratio: [9:16 / 4:5 / 3:4]

Create a high-end fashion editorial visual for [BRAND], based on the theme [THEME], with the focus on [PRODUCT OR SUBJECT]. The output should feel like a premium brand campaign / fashion magazine editorial / lookbook direction, with a strong sense of art direction, typography, layout, and brand mood. This is not a generic fixed template. The composition, typography, image styling, and layout should be designed around the brand mood: [BRAND MOOD]. Main colors should follow [COLOR PALETTE].

The visual style should be clean, elevated, editorial, premium, fashion-forward, and highly designed. Use realistic fashion photography aesthetics, refined lighting, strong negative space, elegant composition, and a clear hierarchy between image, typography, and white space. Keep the overall feeling magazine-like, brand-driven, and visually collectible.

Use [DIRECTION TYPE] as the layout structure:

 If Giant typography campaign: create a bold editorial poster with oversized typography as a major visual element. Let the headline [HEADLINE] interact with the model or product. Use powerful type placement, strong composition, and a premium campaign feel.
 If Couture magazine cover: create a refined fashion cover with a strong central figure or hero product, elegant masthead-style typography, and a polished couture editorial mood. Add a few short editorial text elements such as [SUBHEADLINE] and [EXTRA SMALL TEXT].
 If Accessories editorial page: create a fashion accessories-focused editorial page featuring [PRODUCT OR SUBJECT], with a layout that feels like a premium magazine spread or branded product story. The product should be clearly featured, with elegant typography and supporting editorial text.
 If Lookbook collage spread: create a stylish editorial collage layout using multiple fashion images within one page, arranged like a premium lookbook spread. Keep the collage controlled, minimal, and fashion-oriented, not messy. Use [HEADLINE] and [SUBHEADLINE] as the key editorial text.

Typography should feel intentional and premium. Use large elegant serif or fashion-style typography, with smaller supporting editorial text. Main headline: [HEADLINE]. Subheadline: [SUBHEADLINE]. Optional small text: [EXTRA SMALL TEXT]. Text should be clean and readable, and should support the visual instead of overpowering it.

If a model is included, use [MODEL DESCRIPTION] and style the fashion image to match the brand mood. The model should look editorial, believable, and premium, not like a generic commercial stock model. If the image is product-focused, make the product the hero and support it with strong layout and campaign styling.

The final image should look suitable for brand moodboards, campaign mockups, early brand concepts, editorial poster design, social media visuals, or lookbook exploration.

Avoid: cheap e-commerce look, template-looking layouts, cluttered composition, low-end poster design, excessive text, random decorations, childish styling, weak typography, stock-photo feeling, messy collage, cartoon look, unrealistic anatomy, deformed hands, distorted products, bad text rendering, and real copyrighted magazine logos.

Generate one finished image only in [ASPECT RATIO].

Prompt template for the full 4-image brand proposal:

Create a complete restaurant brand proposal for one fictional brand.

Important:
Generate each page as a separate standalone image.
Do NOT combine the 4 pages into one collage.
Do NOT merge all pages into one poster.
Each image should be independent, but all 4 images must keep the same brand name, logo direction, color palette, typography style, and visual language.

Brand setup:
Brand name: [BRAND NAME]
English name: [ENGLISH BRAND NAME]
Brand type: [bagel & coffee / bakery / café / tea shop / light meal brand]
Positioning: [urban breakfast brand / healthy light meal brand / grab-and-go café]
Target audience: [city commuters / young office workers / lifestyle consumers]
Slogan: [BRAND SLOGAN]
Visual style: clean, fresh, youthful, commercial, premium, professional brand proposal style
Color palette: [cream white + sky blue + bakery yellow + latte brown + small accent color]

Page 1 — Brand Identity System

Generate one vertical 4:5 brand proposal page.

This page should show the brand identity system, including:

* Logo design
* Brand name
* English name
* Slogan
* Brand positioning
* Color palette
* Typography system
* Icon system
* Graphic elements
* Small product hints

The logo should be simple, recognizable, and related to the brand category.
The layout should feel like a professional design studio brand identity board.
Use clean grids, generous white space, clear hierarchy, and premium editorial composition.

Page 2 — Packaging & Product System

Generate one vertical 4:5 brand proposal page.

This page should show the packaging and product system, including:

* Paper shopping bag
* Takeaway box
* Coffee cup
* Cup sleeve
* Product label
* Seal sticker
* Wrapping paper
* Product card
* Realistic food product photography

The packaging should use the same logo, colors, graphic elements, and slogan from Page 1.
Make the food look fresh, realistic, and appetizing.
The page should feel like a commercial packaging proposal, not a discount flyer.

Page 3 — Menu & Ordering System

Generate one vertical 4:5 brand proposal page.

This page should show the menu and ordering system, including:

* Mobile ordering UI
* Menu board
* Product categories
* Product cards
* Prices
* Recommendation tags
* Combo set section
* Small icons and labels

Example menu categories:
Bagel / Coffee / Light Meal / Yogurt / Set

Example labels:
Bestseller / New / Fresh Today / Morning Set / Takeaway

The layout should feel clear, usable, and commercially realistic.
It should look like a real restaurant ordering system inside a brand proposal.

Page 4 — Storefront & Brand Touchpoints

Generate one vertical 4:5 brand proposal page.

This page should show the brand applied in a real store environment, including:

* Storefront signage
* Window stickers
* Counter area
* Menu wall
* Staff apron
* Takeaway bag
* Table card
* Receipt
* Membership card
* Social promo card

The store should feel bright, clean, modern, and realistic.
Keep the same brand identity from the previous pages.
The image should look like the final application page of a complete restaurant brand case study.

Overall requirements:

* 4 separate images
* One page per image
* Same brand across all pages
* Same logo direction
* Same color palette
* Same typography feeling
* Same graphic language
* Professional Behance / Zcool-style brand case study
* Clean modular layout
* Commercially usable design
* Mostly readable text
* No messy collage
* No cheap poster style
* No random unrelated elements

prompt_records.prompt_text:
Vertical 9:16, ultra-realistic top-down photography. An open [Manga Type] lies on a deep walnut wooden desk, with clean black-and-white manga panels, speech bubbles, and character line art. The manga content revolves around [Main Character], showing their 2D manga version, related actions, emotional close-ups, and matching story moments, so it feels like the real character originally belonged inside the manga.

A real adult character materializes from the manga page, lying or half-pushing up on the open book as the main subject. The character wears [Outfit] in the style of [school uniform heroine / romance heroine / detective girl / magical girl / other theme]. Realistic skin texture, natural hair strands, believable clothing folds. The face is slightly lifted, looking directly up toward the top-down camera, making clear eye contact with the reader. The expression is natural, vivid, and emotionally present.

The body, hair, arms, clothes, skirt, and legs must physically interact with the manga pages, with realistic contact shadows, slight paper compression, and subtle page bending. Black-and-white manga pages + full-color 3D character create a strong 2D-to-3D manga-to-reality illusion.

Add an adult male hand in the foreground, naturally holding or turning one corner of the page, with clean short nails. Keep the wooden desk lived-in but minimal, with only a few edge props such as a pen, bookmark, mug rim, or another manga volume corner. Realistic photography, high detail, paper texture, top-down view, sharp focus.

Avoid floating, bad hands, extra fingers, distorted legs or feet, weak eye contact, chaotic panels, too many props, cluttered desk, low detail, plastic skin, CGI look, childlike or underage appearance.

prompt_records.prompt_text:
Create a high-end fashion editorial cover with strong typography, refined negative space and realistic fashion photography.

Theme: [fashion cover / lookbook / artist visual / editorial concept]
Direction: [top-view graphic figure poster / giant initial editorial cover / monochrome cinematic editorial / refined lookbook portrait cover]
Title: [main title]
Subtitle: [short subtitle]
Brand / magazine name: [name]
Subject: [model / artist / portrait / fashion look]
Mood: [minimal / cinematic / refined / quiet / graphic / high-design / editorial]
Color palette: [black-white / cream-black / soft grey / monochrome / neutral tones]
Aspect ratio: [9:16]

The image should feel like a premium fashion magazine cover, editorial poster or designer lookbook page.

Use oversized serif typography, clean negative space, realistic fashion photography, refined posing, strong visual hierarchy, small editorial text blocks, subtle paper texture and a controlled layout.

Choose one direction:

1. Top-view graphic figure poster
   Use a high-angle / top-view full-body fashion portrait on a clean white background. Add thin graphic lines, oversized cropped typography and a strong editorial layout.

2. Giant initial editorial cover
   Use one huge serif letter as the main visual structure. Let the model interact with the letter through overlap, leaning, stepping or partial masking. Keep the background minimal and elegant.

3. Monochrome cinematic editorial
   Use a black-and-white cinematic photo inside a clean magazine-style layout. Add a huge masthead, strong white space and small editorial credits.

prompt_records.prompt_text:

[Theme]: ____
[Chinese Main Title]: ____
[English Title]: ____
[Left Main Subject]: ____
[Right Main Subject]: ____
[Central Axis Content]: Title / Figure / Plant / Negative Space / Other ____
[Clipping Method]: Arc Negative Shape / Spatial Perspective / Flexible Material / Dual Object Counterweight / Other ____
[Background Main Color]: ____
[Main Subject Material and Style]: ____
[Date / Venue]: ____
[Image Ratio]: 9:16

Generate a "central axis clipping" poster with strong visual impact and a sophisticated cultural exhibition vibe.

First establish a clear, stable vertical central axis, then have the [Left Main Subject] and [Right Main Subject] from both sides of the frame jointly form visual weight, pushing the main title, figures, plants, or negative space area toward the center.

The left and right subjects must be sufficiently large, close to the frame edges and allow natural cropping, jointly bearing the primary visual weight. The two sides can differ in outlines, sizes, colors, materials, and details, but the overall visual weight must be balanced, avoiding simple duplication and mechanical mirroring.

Select different clipping methods based on the theme:

Circular or arc-shaped subjects can use outlines to jointly clip out a central negative shape;
Spatial subjects like architecture or screens can form a deep central axis through perspective;
Flexible materials like fabrics or plants can create soft clipping through natural bending;
Objects, figures, or artifacts can reinforce the central title through left-right counterweighting.

The central axis must become the most important reading area of the frame. Use bold large font sizes for the Chinese main title, which can employ vertical layout, horizontal-vertical mixed arrangement, scale variations, partial occlusion, or slight interweaving with the subjects, allowing Typography to truly participate in the composition rather than simply placing it at the top.

Allow the central axis to incorporate a low-weight visual node, such as an extremely small figure, flower branch, pattern rubbing, structural sketch, or research diagram, giving the center both focus and layering without forming a third subject of equal rank.

Information density can be rich but concentrated in 2–3 areas: central axis core information, left and right sidebars, and bottom exhibition details. Create a clear font size contrast between oversized titles and tiny text—do not scatter small text evenly across the entire frame.

Use a clear large-area main color to establish recognition, such as vermilion red, cobalt blue, lemon yellow, grass green, cyan blue, deep brown, or persimmon orange. Overall control within 3–5 main colors, forming contrast through subject materials, Typography, and minimal accent colors.

Core Principle: Not simple "left-right symmetry," but using visual weight from both sides to jointly shape the center. Left and right handle the pressure, central axis handles the focus; structure is stable, but details allow variation.

Overall Requirements: Strong central axis, strong subjects, strong color range; clear design sense, information-rich but not chaotic, sharp edges, clear text, realistic materials, with the polish of a mature cultural exhibition poster and Editorial Design.

Generate a poster with strong visual impact and a sophisticated cultural exhibition ambiance, using a "central axis clamping" composition.  

First establish a clear, stable vertical central axis, then have the left and right subjects jointly apply visual weight toward the center, "clamping" the main title and core information into the focal point of the image.  

The left and right subjects must be sufficiently large, occupying the primary visual weight, and positioned close to the image edges to create a cropping effect. The two sides may differ in form, size, material, and details, but their overall visual weight must be balanced, avoiding mechanical mirroring or simple replication.  

Select the composition method based on the content:  

Bilateral Clamping: Two large subjects approach the center from left and right, with the central axis featuring a massive title.  
Mirror Contrast: Two faces, masks, or character profiles facing each other, forming strong dialogue and tension in the middle.  
Quadrant Array: 4 similar but differently styled subjects arranged around a central vertical title, forming a stable collection array.  
Dual Object Juxtaposition: Two artifacts placed side by side on the left and right, with the central axis establishing order through the title, date, and decorative motifs.  

The Chinese main title must serve as a key visual element, using techniques such as oversized vertical typesetting, mixed horizontal-vertical layouts, partial cropping, or slight overlap with the subjects—avoid simply placing it ordinarily at the top.  

Smaller English text, dates, locations, and exhibition details should be concentrated in 2–3 information zones, creating a stark size contrast with the oversized title. Information density can be rich, but it must be focused and hierarchical, not evenly scattered across the layout.  

Use a large-area solid color background to establish strong brand recognition, such as vermilion red, cobalt blue, lemon yellow, purple, deep brown, or grass green. Limit the overall design to 3–4 primary colors, creating contrast through subject materials, typography, and minimal accent hues.  

Visual style reference: Museum Exhibition Poster × Contemporary Editorial Graphic Design—historical artifacts, figures, cultural relics, or traditional cultural subjects combined with bold, modern, and clear typography.  

Overall requirements: Strong central axis, strong subjects, strong color palette; stable composition without rigidity; rich details without clutter; clear collision between classical content and modern design language.

prompt_records.section_title: 🤯 What to do if there's too much info for a poster using Image2? Use composition references to bring order to high-density layouts!
prompt_records.prompt_text:
Prompt:

[Theme]: ____  
[Chinese Main Title]: ____  
[English Title]: ____  
[Core Main Visual]: ____  
[Irregular Image Method]: Irregular Window / Subject Breaking Frame / Partial Slicing / Image Fusion  
[Corner Pressing Method]: Giant Character Fragments / Dual Corner Insertion / Subject Breaking Frame / Graphic Corner Pressing  
[Auxiliary Visual System]: ____  
[Background Information Layer]: ____  
[Main Color Tone]: ____  
[Accent Color]: ____  
[Date / Institution]: ____  
[Image Ratio]: 9:16  

Create a high-density poster with a strong editorial design feel and cultural exhibition vibe. The core goal is not to reduce information, but to use clear visual hierarchy so that large Chinese text, irregular main images, lines, graphics, small information, and background textures coexist, forming a "chaos within order" layout effect.  

First, establish 1 absolute main visual anchor, then set 2–3 secondary visual anchors. The main visual can use irregular cropping, outline windows, partial frame-breaking, or image fusion—don't just use ordinary rectangular photos. The large Chinese title must truly participate in the composition, such as pressing in from the edges, partial cropping, or interweaving with occlusion from the main image, becoming part of the layout structure, rather than simply pasted next to the image.  

Keep information density medium-high, incorporating Chinese and English titles, dates, institutions, short descriptions, vertical text, partial legends, data, coordinates, lines, or small image slices, but different elements must have obvious scale differences. Create strong jumps in font sizes between extra-large text, medium titles, and tiny information—don't make all text sizes similar, and don't evenly distribute content across the entire frame.  

The entire poster should only use one set of theme-related auxiliary visual language. For example, urban themes use routes and block graphics; conceptual themes use flow lines and image fragments; natural themes use plant line drawings and specimen info; meteorological themes use isobars, wind directions, and radar charts. Don't pile in multiple unrelated decorative sets at once.  

The background must also participate in the design, incorporating very faint patterns, maps, structural diagrams, archival text, data echoes, or material textures to give blank areas content, but the background layer must be distinctly weaker than the main elements.  

Allow text to overlay images, images to break frames, lines to cross zones, and small image slices to stack into the layout; use partial occlusion and incomplete alignment to enhance a postmodern editorial feel, but all elements must organize around the same visual center. Overall, maintain 1 main anchor + 2–3 secondary anchors to avoid true disorder.  

Control colors to 3–5 main hues, establishing a clear color stance—you can pair high-saturation main colors with black and white, or use a unified monochromatic system. Don't let multiple high-saturation colors compete evenly.  

Reading order should be: First glance catches the main subject and large corner-pressing text; second glance discovers irregular images, graphics, and line relationships; third glance reads the date, descriptions, data, and edge information.  

The final effect should resemble a mature cultural exhibition poster, design academy visual, or editorial publication: information-rich, hierarchically complex, with localized collisions, but still retaining a clear visual center when scaled down. Don't make it into an infographic PPT, and don't randomly fill the frame just to seem "complex."

Prompt:

[Theme]: ____  
[Chinese Main Title]: ____  
[English Title]: ____  
[Central Subject]: ____  
[Corner Pressing Method]: Four-Corner Text Press / Diagonal Double-Corner Press / Triangular Encirclement Press + One Corner Release / Single-Corner Heavy Press + Diagonal Response  
[Corner Elements]: Large Chinese Characters / Color Blocks / Information Areas / Patterns  
[Auxiliary Patterns]: ____  
[Main Color Scheme]: ____  
[Accent Color]: ____  
[Date / Institution]: ____  
[Aspect Ratio]: 9:16  

Generate a poster featuring a "corner pressing composition" with the temperament of a mature cultural exhibition and Editorial Graphic Design.  

The core is not simply placing text in the four corners, but using large typography, color blocks, information areas, or patterns along the edges of the image to apply visual pressure inward, naturally "clamping" the central subject into focus.  

Keep the central subject intact, stable, and with clear visual weight—do not deliberately tilt or distort it to fit the composition. The subject should bear approximately 40%–60% of the visual weight.  

Organize the layout according to the [Corner Pressing Method]:  

Four-Corner Text Press:  
Visual elements in all four corners, but with clear primary and secondary hierarchy—1–2 corners bear the main weight, while the others serve only as support, avoiding equal size across all four.  

Diagonal Double-Corner Press:  
Select two diagonal corners as primary pressure points, using large titles or color blocks to clamp the subject from two directions, with the other two corners featuring only small-scale information.  

Triangular Encirclement Press + One Corner Release:  
Three corners form a visual enclosure, while the fourth corner is deliberately kept lighter to give the composition a sense of breathing room.  

Single-Corner Heavy Press + Diagonal Response:  
One corner uses oversized text or strong color blocks to bear the primary pressure, with the diagonal corner responding using smaller elements, while the central subject remains stable.  

The large Chinese title must actively participate in the composition—it can be partially cropped at edges, aligned to borders, or lightly overlaid with the subject, but must remain clearly readable.  

Smaller text such as the English title, date, institution, and theme descriptions should be concentrated in 2–3 areas, forming a clear typographic hierarchy with oversized Chinese, medium titles, and tiny information.  

The background cannot be completely blank; incorporate extremely subtle patterns, archival details, structural diagrams, material textures, or explanatory remnants related to the theme to make the negative space "content-rich," without overpowering the subject.  

The entire poster should use only one set of primary auxiliary patterns, which must have a genuine connection to the theme; limit colors to 3–5 main ones, with a clear color stance for the whole piece.  

Overall information density should be medium-high, but with clear visual hierarchy:  
First glance: See the subject and corner pressing relationship;  
Second glance: Notice the large Chinese title;  
Third glance: Read the English, date, and auxiliary information.  

Each poster must have a complete theme and authentic content expression—avoid excessive meaningless placeholder text. Even without the fine print, it should stand as a complete visual work.  

Overall effect: A cultural exhibition poster, magazine editorial design, mature printed publication vibe—with pressure at the edges, focus at the center, rich yet orderly.
